purpose: Canonical owner-approved complementary semantic directions for Friends synastry. These rows supersede the same canonical pair keys at relationship-bundle assembly time without duplicating pair identities.

rows.body_you: The way {{Name}} naturally shows up can make you feel more like yourself. Something about their manner, their confidence, or the way they move through a situation may bring your own personality forward without much effort. You may feel seen by them before either of you has said very much. That can be affirming, but it can also make their reaction matter too much. Enjoy how easy it is to be yourself without needing their attention to tell you that you are getting it right.
rows.body_they: {{holder1}} tends to notice you when you enter a situation, and their response to how you present yourself can make you feel seen enough to speak more directly about what you want. Because their confidence carries so much weight with you, you may start checking their reaction before making your own decision. Your body knows the difference between speaking for yourself and waiting for their response, and you can feel it in how you hold yourself.

rows.body_you: The way {{Name}} naturally reacts can rub against the way you see yourself. A look, a tone, or the way they handle a situation may make you feel misunderstood before they have actually criticized you. You may respond by explaining yourself more forcefully or trying to prove who you are. The connection gets harder when every difference in style starts feeling like a judgment of your character.
rows.body_they: {{holder1}} often sets the tone or direction before you have had room to show how you want to come across. You may explain your choices more firmly or push back, which can lead them to press their point again. Repeating that pattern can leave you feeling crowded out and them feeling challenged.

rows.body_you: {{Name}}’s natural way of being tends to make your own confidence easier to access. You do not have to work very hard to feel understood around them, and their reactions usually leave you more comfortable saying what you want or showing more of who you are. Their presence does not make you feel like you need to polish yourself first. You can relax and let more of your personality come through.
rows.body_they: When {{holder1}} is clear about who they are and what they want, you feel more comfortable being yourself while meeting people or entering a new situation. As you relax and respond more naturally, it becomes easier for {{holder1}} to keep expressing themselves clearly.

rows.body_you: {{Name}}’s ambition can wake up your own. Seeing what they are building, what they want to be known for, or how seriously they take their direction may make you think more clearly about the person you want to become. Their public life can pull more confidence and purpose out of you. Just be careful not to measure your own worth by how useful you are to their climb or how closely your life matches the path they are on.
rows.body_they: {{holder1PossCap}} Sun lands on {{holder2Poss}} Midheaven, and one person's whole way of being points at the other's finish line. Mentorship happens here without anyone applying for it: visibility rubs off, direction rubs back. The risk is fusion, where one career quietly becomes both people's project. Admire, assist, and keep separate nameplates.

rows.body_you: {{Name}}’s goals can make you look harder at your own direction. Their work, recognition, or plans for the future may stir up comparison, especially when they seem certain about where they are going and you are still figuring something out. You may want to prove that your path matters too, or start treating their success like a verdict on your own. Their climb is not a scorecard. Let it show you what you want without turning it into proof that you are behind.
rows.body_they: {{holder1PossCap}} Sun sits at a hard angle to {{holder2Poss}} Midheaven, and it plays out as identity versus trajectory. What one is keeps questioning where the other is headed, so career advice arrives sounding like a verdict on the whole person. Underneath, both want the same thing: to matter on their own terms. Keep the lanes labeled: one life, one climb, two owners.

rows.body_you: {{Name}}’s direction can make your own ambition easier to admit. Seeing them take their work seriously may remind you to put your name on what you are good at, ask for the opportunity, or stop pretending a goal does not matter to you. Their progress does not have to compete with yours. Sometimes watching someone build something they care about makes your own future feel more possible.
rows.body_they: {{holder1PossCap}} Sun backs {{holder2Poss}} Midheaven without either trying: confidence feeding the climb, alliance without paperwork. Introductions, references, honest reads: all of it flows and lands. Professional goodwill this frictionless is rare; spend it in both directions.

rows.body_you: {{Name}} may treat you like the kind of person they naturally want beside them. Their way of partnering can make your strengths feel especially visible, and being chosen that clearly can bring out more confidence in you. The risk is that the fit feels so good that you start becoming the role they respond to best. You can be important to {{Name}} without turning yourself into their idea of the perfect partner, friend, or collaborator.
rows.body_they: {{holder1PossCap}} Sun lands on {{holder2Poss}} Descendant, the spot where {{holder2Poss}} chart describes an ideal other. One walks in already shaped like what the other tends to seek, so the alliance feels cast rather than chosen. That fit is real and it carries expectations with it: nobody can be a role and a person at once for long. Enjoy the casting, then keep meeting the actual human.

rows.body_you: What {{Name}} expects from a close relationship may not always fit the way you naturally operate. They may want more compromise, more availability, or a different kind of partnership than you instinctively offer. That can make you feel like being yourself is somehow the problem, so you either defend yourself harder or start changing to keep the connection working. A relationship can have expectations without requiring one person to disappear inside them.
rows.body_they: {{holder1PossCap}} Sun sits at a hard angle to {{holder2Poss}} Descendant, so one person's way of being crosses the other's picture of a good partner. Cooperation keeps requiring translation: leading feels like dominating, independence feels like distance. Nobody is auditioning for the partner seat, which is exactly the friction. Stop comparing the friendship to the template and it improves overnight.

rows.body_you: The way {{Name}} partners with people tends to work well with who you already are. You may feel wanted without feeling managed, and included without having to become easier, quieter, or more agreeable first. Their idea of cooperation fits your personality well enough that working together does not cost you your voice. Partnership does not require an audition here.
rows.body_they: {{holder1PossCap}} Sun supports {{holder2Poss}} Descendant: presence and partnership on friendly terms. Cooperation feels dignified here: help without hierarchy, alliance without auditions. Team up often; the results flatter both.

rows.body_you: Being close to {{Name}}’s private world can bring out a version of you that does not need an audience. Their home, family stories, or the way they are when nobody is watching may make you feel trusted enough to drop some of your own armor. You can feel more like yourself in the quiet parts of this connection. Just remember that being welcomed inside does not make their private life yours to manage or explain for them.
rows.body_they: {{holder1PossCap}} Sun lands on {{holder2Poss}} IC, so one person gets waved past the lobby. Home privileges arrive early here: the couch, the family stories, the version with no company manners. Being let that far in is trust, not convenience. Treat the inside information like the valuables they are.

rows.body_you: {{Name}}’s need for privacy, quiet, or familiar routines can sometimes make your natural way of showing up feel like too much. You may want more conversation, movement, or openness just when they want to pull back into what feels familiar. That difference can make you feel rejected when they are actually trying to recover. You do not have to dim yourself, but you may have to learn when their closed door is about rest and not about you.
rows.body_they: {{holder1PossCap}} Sun sits at a hard angle to {{holder2Poss}} IC, so one person's shine disturbs the other's quiet. Visibility and privacy want different rooms: one livens the house, the other guards its stillness, and both feel judged for it. Neither mode is a flaw; they are different recoveries. Match the energy to the evening, not to the habit.

rows.body_you: {{Name}}’s private world can make it easier for you to put down the version of yourself that is always doing, proving, or being seen. Around them, ordinary things can feel good: a quiet meal, a long conversation, sitting together without needing to make the time impressive. Their sense of home gives your confidence somewhere to rest. You do not always have to shine to know you still belong.
rows.body_they: {{holder1PossCap}} Sun supports {{holder2Poss}} IC: presence that makes the private world brighter without crowding it. Visits lift the house instead of costing it. Rare guest physics. Use liberally.

rows.body_you: {{Name}}’s vulnerable places can make you much more aware of the effect you have on them. You may notice that your confidence, success, or even a casual comment lands more deeply than you expected, and that can make you want to protect them. The danger is starting to dim yourself so they never have to feel uncomfortable. Their pain deserves care, but your light is not the injury. You can be gentle without becoming smaller.
rows.body_they: {{holder1PossCap}} Sun sits right on {{holder2Poss}} Chiron, so one person's shine lands on the other's oldest bruise. Simply being confident can ache to watch when the watcher's wound is about worth. Nobody is doing anything wrong; proximity is the whole mechanism. Handled gently, this heals: the wounded side borrows courage, the bright side learns what light costs.

rows.body_you: {{Name}}’s pain can make you question parts of yourself that normally feel simple. If your confidence, choices, or success touches an old wound for them, you may feel guilty for shining or defensive because you never meant to hurt them. That can turn their sensitivity into something you feel responsible for fixing. Be kind with the sore spot, but do not confuse being considerate with having to apologize for who you are.
rows.body_they: {{holder1PossCap}} Sun sits at a hard angle to {{holder2Poss}} Chiron, and confidence keeps scraping an old ache. Wins land wrong: one celebrates and the other hears an echo of every time they came second. The flinch is history, not envy, and calling it envy wounds twice. Celebrate carefully, flinch honestly, and say both quiet parts out loud.

rows.body_you: {{Name}}’s vulnerability can make your confidence gentler without making it weaker. You may become more thoughtful about how you encourage them, more aware of what a certain subject costs them, and better at knowing when to stand beside them instead of trying to cheer them out of the feeling. Their softer places teach you that strength does not have to enter every situation at full volume.
rows.body_they: {{holder1PossCap}} Sun warms {{holder2Poss}} Chiron without pressing on it. Confidence rubs off gently here; the wounded place gets sunlight instead of spotlight. Healing happens as a side effect of company. Keep showing up; that is the whole treatment.

rows.body_you: Watching {{Name}} grow can make you more aware of the person you are becoming too. Their next steps may pull qualities out of you that were already there but easier to ignore: more courage, more visibility, or a stronger willingness to choose your own direction. You may feel important in their growth, but do not turn their future into your assignment. You can inspire each other without becoming responsible for where the other person ends up.
rows.body_they: {{holder1PossCap}} Sun sits right on {{holder2Poss}} North Node, so one person is a walking preview of where the other is headed. The admiration has direction built into it: what one is, the other is becoming. Mentorship happens by osmosis, invited or not. Make it explicit and it accelerates.

rows.body_you: The direction {{Name}} is growing toward may challenge the version of yourself you are used to being around them. As they take new risks, change priorities, or move away from an old dynamic, you may have to figure out who you are without the familiar role you had in their life. Their growth is not a rejection of you. It may simply be showing you that you are changing too.
rows.body_they: {{holder1PossCap}} Sun sits at a hard angle to {{holder2Poss}} North Node, and one person's way of being complicates the other's becoming. The example is magnetic and slightly off-course: following it means drifting from the assignment. Admire without copying. Two different futures can share one friendship.

rows.body_you: {{Name}}’s growth tends to bring out a good kind of confidence in you. When they try something new, take themselves more seriously, or move toward a bigger life, you may feel more willing to do the same in your own way. Their becoming does not make you feel left behind. It reminds you that you are allowed to keep becoming too.
rows.body_they: {{holder1PossCap}} Sun backs {{holder2Poss}} North Node: presence that makes the other's growth feel possible. Encouragement lands here without pressure, example without homework. Growth-friendly company is rare. Keep it close during the big stretches.

rows.body_you: {{Name}} can make you feel known very quickly. Something about their history, habits, or the way they respond to you may bring out a version of yourself that already knows how to behave here. That familiarity can feel warm and effortless, but it can also pull you back into an old role before you notice. Enjoy being known without assuming you have to keep being the person they first recognized.
rows.body_they: {{holder1PossCap}} Sun sits right on {{holder2Poss}} South Node, and the recognition was instant: this person again, somehow, finally. Comfort and familiarity arrive before biography does. The sweetness is real; the risk is nostalgia running the friendship. Enjoy the old warmth and point it at new things.

rows.body_you: {{Name}} may bring out an older version of you that you thought you had already left behind. Their habits, expectations, or the way they remember you can make it easy to slip back into being the fixer, the responsible one, the easygoing one, or whatever role once kept things working. Familiar does not always mean current. You are allowed to show them who you are now, even if the old version was easier for both of you.
rows.body_they: {{holder1PossCap}} Sun sits at a hard angle to {{holder2Poss}} South Node, so one person's presence keeps tugging the other backward. Around this brightness, old habits feel rewarded: the easy role, the retired self, the outgrown script. The affection is real; the regression is optional. Enjoy the history, then act your current age.

rows.body_you: {{Name}}’s familiarity can make it easy to relax into yourself. You may not need to explain your humor, your habits, or the version of you that comes out when you are tired and nobody is trying to impress anyone. There is comfort in being known without a long introduction. Just keep making new memories too, so the relationship stays connected to who you are now and not only who you have already been.
rows.body_they: {{holder1PossCap}} Sun eases {{holder2Poss}} South Node: comfortable brightness, no demands attached. Being known this thoroughly and liked anyway is the gift here. It restores rather than stretches, and that is a legitimate job. Rest in it.

rows.body_you: {{Name}}’s refusal to pretend can bring out a more honest version of you. Around them, you may feel less willing to smile through something you dislike, play a role that does not fit, or make yourself easier for everyone else to handle. Their rawness can make it easier for you to say what you actually mean. Just make sure honesty is helping you become more yourself, not turning every difference into a test of who is braver.
rows.body_they: {{holder1PossCap}} Sun sits right on {{holder2Poss}} Lilith, so one person's daylight lands on the other's wild territory. The unedited side gets seen, plainly and without flinching, which reads as either liberation or exposure depending on the day. Respect makes the difference. Witness without taming and this becomes fiercely loyal.

rows.body_you: {{Name}}’s bluntness can hit the part of you that wants to be respected and understood. When they reject a rule, call something out, or refuse to soften their opinion, you may hear more of a challenge to you than they actually meant. That can make you defend your position or try to prove that your way is legitimate. Their refusal does not automatically make your identity the target. Let them say no without turning the no into a verdict on you.
rows.body_they: {{holder1PossCap}} Sun sits at a hard angle to {{holder2Poss}} Lilith, and the respectable keeps provoking the raw. One's polish reads as pretense, one's bluntness reads as sabotage, and both verdicts overreach. Each holds a piece the other rations: legitimacy and honesty. Trade instead of prosecuting.

rows.body_you: {{Name}}’s honesty can make it easier for you to stop polishing yourself for approval. Their willingness to be direct about what they want, dislike, or will not accept may make you more comfortable doing the same. You do not have to become louder or more rebellious to benefit from it. Sometimes freedom is simply realizing you can be fully yourself and the connection does not fall apart.
rows.body_they: {{holder1PossCap}} Sun accepts {{holder2Poss}} Lilith without a struggle: the raw side is simply welcome in this light. No taming attempted, none needed. That acceptance is rarer than either realizes. Name it once so it is never accidental.
